findings.claim: The table row for unreadable frontmatter now lists 'no two --- lines at all (a leading BOM, blank line or spaces included)' as a cause, but the quoted count label and reason text still say only '(CRLF line endings or no closing ---)'. A reader matching program output against the table gets a label that does not describe the newly documented cases.

The paragraph on frontmatter reading is hard to follow: the first sentence says frontmatter is read between two '---' lines, then 'any other page is read whole', with a parenthetical nested inside a long sentence about plain-text pages being refused. It also differs in wording from the README ('no readable frontmatter ... whatever its first line'). Splitting it into short sentences would help.

The note-format sentence was reflowed so that the long literal 'note: N page(s)...' string now sits on one over-long line mid-paragraph, and the new vault-wide-count rule is added after the 'no page is hidden' sentence, mixing the single-project rule with the multi-project rule. 'Top-level line' is also undefined for readers.

evidence: Diff only touches two docs files; no code was visible, so the doc claims about behavior could not be verified against the implementation.
The README and guide wording were compared against each other and against the unchanged label strings in the table.
